> For my warm-up project, I am designing a simple, customized USB-powered desk light using individual LEDs! It will be portable and powered by a simple 5V USB-C breakout board. The circuit should split into 3 separate paths to 3 separate 5mm colored LEDs: blue, white, and green. I'll connect a physical push-button switch to turn the system on and off. I will also add 220-ohm resistors in front of each light to prevent the system from burning out. Everything will be arranged on the breadboard.

### 2026-10-04 — This is my first time with Hack Club. I spent 3 hours joining the Slack, researching what kind of project to make, what parts I need, where to find them, and how to assemble my parts in Tinkercad! I k

**3h**

This is my first time with Hack Club. I spent 3 hours joining the Slack, researching what kind of project to make, what parts I need, where to find them, and how to assemble my parts in Tinkercad! I know I didn't "get much done" objectively, but I spent a lot of time today figuring out how to make robotics accessible to me by visually mocking them up and understanding what supplies I need. Joining the Slack helped me meet a lot of similarly ambitious people! My final Tinkercad mockup (on GitHub) might not be the most accurate, but I tried, and I hope I get positive, constructive feedback on how to fix it! I'm so excited for my Half-Life journey!
